notes: Corrected: לְעֵינֶיךָ was split as *unto* on the preposition with עַיִן `unrepresented`. One English word is written for the preposition and its construct noun, so rule 30's compound-preposition sentence fuses them, headed on עַיִן (rule 23); the suffix keeps *thee*. Contrast DEU.25.9, where the ASV writes *in* and *the presence* and the split stands.
Two supplied words remain `added`: the *if* of *lest if*, which פֶּן cannot hold a second time (rules 51, 55), and the *and* of *and beat him*, for which no conjunction morpheme stands (rule 14).
The supplied *with* of *with many stripes* stays on מַכָּה under rule 33; giving it to רַבָּה was the materially competing reading.
